subject: Post-call: Hosting matrix + migration exit-paths
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpro.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — hosting options & migration questions

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope the next technical deep-dive:

Summary from our call:
- FinPro is evaluating Redwood for customer-facing synthesis and internal batch scoring.
- Primary requirement: predictable latency for interactive queries; some regulated workloads require strict VPC/on-prem constraints.
- Migration sources: a combination of a legacy GPU cluster for nightly batch jobs + an internal self-hosted LLM gateway used by a handful of services.
- Initial preference mentioned: Dedicated capacity for production traffic, with a Private VPC option for regulated datasets.

Key follow-ups / asks (so our infra proposal aligns):
1) Traffic profile: can you confirm peak QPS and average request size (tokens)? We heard ~150 req/min peak but want confirmation.
2) Data residency: which datasets must remain in customer VPC / on-prem? Is it full model payloads or only PII?
3) Authentication / SSO: do you need SAML/SCIM for both hosted and private control plane?
4) Migration constraints: any blocker to taking an exported model or do you require us to run inside your environment?
5) Procurement timeline & budget owner: who should we loop in for contract/PO discussions?

Attachments: redwood-hosting-matrix.pdf (hosting feature comparison) and finpro-migration-checklist.xlsx (starter checklist). Please review; I highlighted the items relevant to Dedicated vs Private.

Next steps proposed:
- Technical deep-dive (runtime & migration): 60–90 minutes — would Aditya be the right engineer to lead?
- If you confirm constraints above, we’ll produce a short proposal with architecture options and cost ranges.

Available times for a deep-dive: Tue 9/7 10–12 PT, Wed 9/8 9–11 PT.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0142

---
(Attachment stubs: redwood-hosting-matrix.pdf (8 pages), finpro-migration-checklist.xlsx)

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpro.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@finpro.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2027 17:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — hosting options & migration questions

Thanks Jasmine — this is helpful. Quick answers below: 

- Peak traffic: we see bursts up to ~150 requests per minute for the UI, average payload ~600 tokens. Nightly batch jobs hit the legacy GPU cluster (models are larger, longer context).
- Data residency: regulated PHI-like datasets must stay inside our VPC for now; non-sensitive logs can flow to hosted. We would like the ability to route only regulated traffic to a private deployment.
- SSO: yes, SAML/SCIM required for corporate users.
- Migration: we prefer to keep models in our environment initially — we have an internal gateway wrapping a combination of open and licensed models; goal is to retire the gateway but we cannot export certain licensed models.
- Procurement timeline: aiming to select vendor by end of Q3; procurement contact is cc'd.

We are leaning towards Dedicated for most workloads (predictable throughput) plus a Private/VPC deployment for regulated traffic. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports hybrid routing (some traffic to hosted/dedicated, some to private) and whether you can peer with our VPC?

A technical deep-dive on Wed 9/8 at 10am PT works for us.

—Alex
Alex Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, FinPro Analytics
alex.chen@finpro.com | (212) 555-0199

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpro.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 4 Sep 2027 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — hosting options & migration questions

Alex — thanks for the quick answers. Adding a few technical notes ahead of Wednesday's deep-dive so we can be efficient: 

1) Hybrid routing: supported. Policy-based routing can split by route/model/customer tag. Typical pattern: interactive UI -> Dedicated (low-latency pool) and regulated endpoints -> Private VPC (peered or on-prem). We also support automatic fallback to hosted variants if capacity is constrained.

2) VPC connectivity: we offer VPC peering and private link options for Dedicated and a fully private control plane for Private deployments. For on-prem, we ship an appliance that runs the inference runtime and registers to the customer's control plane.

3) Migration of models / gateway: two approaches depending on licensing:
   - If models can be exported: we recommend an initial POC running the exported model inside your private deployment to validate latency and cost.
   - If models cannot be exported: we can set up transparent routing from your gateway to Redwood inference endpoints (Dedicated or Private) while keeping the licensed weights in your cluster; this requires a small adapter but avoids weight export.

4) Batch jobs & KV cache: Nightly large-context jobs are a different cost profile; suggest keeping batch workloads on the legacy cluster initially and incrementally moving use-cases to Dedicated. We can containerize the batch runner to replicate GPU harness. Also plan KV cache warming for migration to reduce cold-starts.

5) Compliance artifacts: we will prepare the SOC2 + encryption + logging pack for procurement. I will attach the preliminary checklist and an example architecture diagram in the deep-dive follow-up.

Preliminary risk areas to discuss on Wed: network egress for private traffic, model-licensing constraints, and performance under long-context batch workloads.

Proposed attendees: technical leads for infra, platform, and procurement.

Thanks — Aditya
Aditya Rao
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | (650) 555-0201

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — hosting options & migration questions

Perfect — thanks Aditya and Jasmine. Wed 9/8 10:00am PT confirmed for the tech deep-dive. Attendees on our side: myself, infra lead (Maya Patel), and procurement (cc).

Action items before the call:
- Jasmine: please send SOC2/security pack and NDA link so procurement can review.
- Aditya: please share a short migration playbook + any example latency numbers for dedicated vs private for 600-token payloads.
- Alex (us): we'll gather licensing constraints and a short list of models that cannot be exported.

Procurement expects an initial commercial signal by end of next week; we'll aim to provide an internal readiness note after the deep-dive.

See you Wednesday.

—Alex
